!!! DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE unless you know what you are doing !!!
If you get stuck with this config, please open an issue or get in touch via the discord.
Here are some of the variables you may want to change:
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT - You can increase this if Global Placement fails with error GPL-0302.
Users have reported that values up to 80 worked well for them.
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 40ns == 25MHz. This chip runs at 25MHz
(the full-rate QSPI controller gates SCK from the 25MHz clk); constraining
at the real operating period keeps the resizer from over-buffering a large
8x2 design and hurting routability. Tighten toward 20ns only if wanted.
Hold slack margin. 8x2 is TT's LARGEST tile, and this design is marginal on
it: clk reaches 3553 sinks across the wide 1378x226 (6:1) die with ~1300um
avg leaf wire -> CTS skew -> a post-CTS hold-buffer FLOOD (2723 @ margin
0.1/0.05; 1224-2057 @ 0.05/0.02, placement-noise dependent) that detailed
placement can't legalize (DPL-0036, ~64-98 stuck instances). Base util is
already 0.612, so density is not a lever and a bigger die is not available.
CTS_CLK_MAX_WIRE_LENGTH=300 was tried and had ZERO effect (avg leaf wire
byte-identical). CORRECTED 2026-07-25: the earlier note here said LibreLane
3.0.3 'did not bind it' -- it DOES. cts.tcl:96 passes it to
repair_clock_nets -max_wire_length. So the null result is a real measurement
of the WRONG lever: it buffers long clock NETS, it does not cluster SINKS,
which is why the ~1300um leaf wire never moved. Config is NOT exhausted --
verified bound in the installed 3.0.3: CTS_SINK_CLUSTERING_SIZE /
_MAX_DIAMETER / _ENABLE (cts.tcl:67-69) attack the leaf wire AT SOURCE;
PL_RESIZER_HOLD_MAX_BUFFER_PCT (rsz_timing_postcts.tcl:47, DEFAULT 50 = the
flood is permitted up to 50% of design size), PL_RESIZER_HOLD_REPAIR_TNS_PCT
(:49) and PL_RESIZER_HOLD_MAX_UTIL_PCT (:50) cap it; GPL_CELL_PADDING /
DPL_CELL_PADDING reserve legal sites for post-CTS insertions (the classic
DPL-0036 fix -- note PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT is set explicitly below, so it
will NOT auto-derive util+5*padding+10; raise both together, deliberately).
PREFER the skew-reducing levers: capping hold repair can leave REAL hold
violations, so any cap that lands must be justified by the post-route hold
report, not by the flow merely completing.
Current setting = post-CTS hold margin 0.05 -> 0.02, which sheds the near-
threshold buffers (real negative-slack holds are still fixed) to try to get
the flood under the legalization limit.
=== THE HOLD-FLOOD STORY ABOVE IS SOLVED. Measured 2026-07-25 from a full
local run at exactly this config: repair_timing found 190 hold endpoints
(not 2086) and inserted 190 hold buffers; detailed placement legalized with
NO DPL-0034/DPL-0036; post-CTS STA hold_vio=0, hold worst slack +0.177ns,
setup_vio=0, setup worst slack +10.5ns. Hold is genuinely MET, not capped --
so none of the hold-capping levers (PL_RESIZER_HOLD_MAX_BUFFER_PCT,
_HOLD_REPAIR_TNS_PCT, _HOLD_MAX_UTIL_PCT) is needed, and using them would
risk leaving REAL hold violations. Leave them at their defaults.
=== THE ACTUAL REMAINING WALL IS ROUTING CONGESTION, not placement.
Same local run: global routing burned all 50/50 overflow iterations and still
ended with [GRT-0115] 'finished with congestion' (total overflow 1461; usage
met1 81%, met2 77%, met3 66%, met4 only 30%). GRT_ALLOW_CONGESTION=1 then
suppresses that failure and hands 183337 congested guides to TritonRoute,
which reported 23312 DRC violations after its first pass (41 min at 20
threads) without converging. THAT is what the 3h40m cancelled CI run was
doing -- a GitHub runner has fewer cores, so it cannot finish inside the
6h job limit. Congestion driver: final instance utilization 0.7196 (base
0.612 + 2262 timing-repair buffers = 21135um2 + 4399 tap cells) on the fixed
6:1 die with only met1-met4 for signal (met5 is reserved for the PDN).
=== DEMAND REDUCTION (this experiment). Of those 2262 repair buffers, ZERO
are setup buffers (setup_buffer=0, hold_buffer=190) -- they are ALL
electrical-rule repair for max-slew/max-cap/max-fanout. And the repair loses
anyway: 90 slew + 247 fanout violations still stand at post-GRT STA. So the
flow is spending 10% of instance area on buffers that neither timing nor the
rule check needs. Both constraints below were self-imposed tightenings:
* MAX_TRANSITION 0.75 -> 1.5ns. 1.5ns is sky130_fd_sc_hd's OWN declared
limit -- the liberty has 'default_max_transition : 1.5' and every cell
pin carries 'max_transition : 1.5'. So 0.75 was a 2x tightening BELOW
the vendor limit, and 1.5 is inside the characterized NLDM tables (not
an extrapolation). At a 40ns period with +10.5ns setup slack, the added
transition delay is absorbed trivially.
* MAX_FANOUT 10 -> 24. The liberty declares NO default_max_fanout, so 10
is purely librelane's own number. Fanout limits are only a PROXY for cap
and slew, and both of those stay directly constrained (0.2pF / 1.5ns).
DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: MAX_CAPACITANCE_CONSTRAINT stays 0.2pF (the real
electrical guard) and DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_SLEW_PCT/_CAP_PCT stay 20 (repair
still builds a 20% margin into what it does insert). Acceptance = util and
GRT overflow must FALL and hold must stay met; judge on the reports, never
on the flow merely completing. If congestion survives this, next lever is
GPL_CELL_PADDING/DPL_CELL_PADDING (both 0 now) raised together with
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT, then an RTL shrink (vga_engine linebuf is 2x20x16 =
640 flops, 18% of all 3552 flops).
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
If you need a custom clock configuration, read the following documentation first:
https://tinytapeout.com/faq/#how-can-i-map-an-additional-external-clock-to-one-of-the-gpios
SCK NOTE: uio_out[3] is a GATED clock (sck = sck_en & ~clk in qspi_ctrl.sv)
that drives ONLY the external cartridge pad -- NO internal register is
clocked by it (all storage is posedge/negedge clk). The base SDC already
constrains it as a clk-launched output via set_output_delay [all_outputs],
so no create_generated_clock is required and CTS never tree-balances it.
Configuration docs: https://librelane.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/configuration.html
